correctness.rationale: For all \(k\ge2\) the edge-cover bound is \(\lceil k/2\rceil\); \(k\le3\) cannot have two surviving distinct diploid types after any allele deletion. COD \(k=4\) is impossible by disjoint-edge vertex count. The DOMCOD \(k=4\) triple lemma forces exactly 23,24,34 and at least two of 12,13,14, giving exactly three optimal sets of size five. At \(k=5\) any three-genotype covering set leaves at most one survivor after some allele deletion; path 12,23,34,45 provides a four-genotype DOMCOD construction. COD \(k=5\) needs a factor-critical five-vertex graph, min degree≥2 and at least five edges, with exactly the twelve labeled five-cycles attaining equality. For even \(k\ge6\) use three-or-more disjoint pairs; for odd \(k\ge7\) use r disjoint pairs plus one edge to the last label, so at least two disjoint types survive every allele deletion. The finite checker exhaustively confirms \(2\le k\le6\) (12,494 assertions) and constructions through \(k=60\); the analytic argument proves all k.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Under COD, genotype edges form a five-vertex factor-critical graph, so the five-cycle minimizer is not independently new. Under pollen-dominant/stigma-codominant SSI, a donor edge is accepted when its dominant lower-rank allele is absent from the recipient edge; compatible pairs may overlap a recessive allele. Thus an undirected matching/factor-critical formulation is not equivalent to the directed four-label and five-label conditions. The full comparative thresholds are not obtained by simply renaming factor-critical graphs.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2009 full study treats the selection and evolution of pollen/stigma-specific allele dominance, and the inspected open 2014 study treats stochastic viability and allele richness. Neither states the adversarial genotype-deletion minimum support law. The 1997 origin paper establishes SSIcod/SSIdomcod phenotypes and simulates allelic turnover, as confirmed in its accessible abstract; full text was not available, so residual priority risk is expressly retained. The known factor-critical characterization supplies the five-cycle COD subcase but cannot imply the directed DOMCOD four- and five-allele cutoffs. Relevant indexed plant–pollinator coextinction and diploid viability-selection results involve different objects, hypotheses and quantified outcomes. The distinct proposed cross-model threshold survives the completed comparisons on a qualified best-knowledge basis.
residual_risks: The original 1997 Schierup et al. article and the 1998 Vekemans et al. mate-availability paper could not be examined in full; their abstracts and citation scope alone do not exclude obscure appendices.
Broader matching or directed-graph extremal formulations could contain an equivalent specific theorem under different terminology.
Biological pollen dominance need not form a strict shared total order across actual populations, so the result is only for the precisely stated idealized model.

value.rationale: S-allele diversity under bottlenecks and mate limitation is a biologically motivated discrete-resilience problem. The exact minimum number of heterozygote types required to retain any compatible cross after losing every carrier of one S-allele is a natural support invariant. The sharp k=4 feasibility gap between pollen dominance and complete codominance, the k=5 difference in exact budgets, and the k≥6 equivalence to basic edge coverage are structural boundaries, not arbitrary tables. The result isolates what dominance adds to support resilience while explicitly disclaiming population viability guarantees.
